notes: The farm, the house and the valley share one frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche in the north gatepost; only the village fire has its own grid.

The house is the owner's one room, 7 by 4 paces (5.25 by 3.0 m) with the hearth FRONT, the doorway RIGHT facing the gate, the sleeping bench BEHIND and the jars and hand mill LEFT, the table at its exact middle.
The niche goes right through the north gatepost, so Eliab lights the lamp from the yard at dusk and sets it back from the road at night, and the flame shows through the house doorway.

The signature move is W20 and W21 in one take, the camera following the lantern out through the gateway between the two sons and stopping in the gateway while the lamp goes down the road into the black valley.
Scene 1A's flash of the old hand cupping the new flame is the middle of W19; Scene 10's flash of the lamp up the black hill with the ewe and the singing comes from W27 and W28.
The ewe handover is the W29 to W30 stitch on her fleece, the camera moving 1.2 m behind it from Asher's shoulder to his front.
W10 cuts to W11 and W27 cuts to W28 on purpose, to fold Asher's walk back to bed and the lantern's long climb into one break each.

Eliab's search goes out by the road, over the valley floor east of the village, up along the black slope to the thorn gully and home up the hill path, so the fire sees his lamp far up the slope behind Asher, about 330 m away.

Amos keeps the night at the threshing floor as at harvest, comes up to the doorway with his sleeves rolled and goes back out to the floor with the bread; Miriam brings the coal because the lamp is lit at every dark.
The midnight meal sits in the doorway's sightline from the fold gate: Micah on a west stool, Eliab pouring beside him, Miriam tearing bread at the table's east side, the dog under the table.
